title: Wartime travel and the reunion of 1946
summary: They discuss buses and trains in wartime and how good it was to have Jo and Walter back.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: All through this war period, it was still a pretty good band.
Yes. Yes.
But, what was life like? I mean, were you having alot of trouble with transportation? How did you move around during the war?
Back during the war we -- let's see -- mostly we travelled by buses. Mostly buses. Buses and trains were our means of transportation.
But, it was a bit rough, wasn't it?
Yes. It was. It was. What year was that now?
Well, I was talking here -- no, I'm getting away from -- but, I was thinking more of -- you know -- like '43, '45, '46.
Oh. I see. Yeah. Way back.
Because, alot of the bands did have trouble.
Yeah. Yeah. During that period I don't think we had the Greyhound situation. I think we had, like, a company over in Jersey we used to use.
Yeah. Well, I thought there were problems, you know, with -- well, when you come into the period when Basie has to break up the band --
Mm.
--what was happening?
That's in the '50's you mean?
Yeah.
Oh, Stanley. You're not going to jump that far ahead are you?
Yes, we are.
Well, why?
Well, I mean, this is where -- when did it happen? It's around 1950.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
Well, I mean, why are you going to -- I mean, you haven't really said very much -- in '46 Joe and Walter come back.
Yeah.
And, the war is over. So, surely it must have been like old times again for awhile there? Wasn't it?
Oh, yeah. It was good to -- you know -- it was good to have them back.
Yeah. Yeah.
Yeah. We had a ball when they came back.
